histology: colon adenocarcinoma (presumed; histologic subtype not specified at intake)
stage: IV (metastatic; liver metastases status post-resection, peritoneal involvement present)

biomarkers.name: Germline hereditary cancer panel
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Multi-gene germline panel (Lynch syndrome genes MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2/EPCAM, APC, MUTYH, others) reported negative; excludes hereditary syndromes from current decision tree.

biomarkers.name: KRAS A59T
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Tissue NGS confirming KRAS A59T with variant allele frequency (clonality), plus co-occurring RAS family (NRAS, HRAS) and BRAF V600 status. A59 mutations are non-canonical RAS-pathway activators and read differently from G12C/G12D for the available KRAS-G12X selective inhibitors; clonality and co-mutations gate anti-EGFR (cetuximab/panitumumab) eligibility.

biomarkers.name: APC E1295
biomarkers.value: mutated (likely truncating; presumed mutation cluster region)
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Confirm exact codon-1295 variant (E1295* vs E1295fs vs missense) and whether the lesion falls in the mutation cluster region (MCR, ~codons 1250-1500). MCR-truncated APC loses beta-catenin downregulation domains; relevant for Wnt-pathway biology and potential tankyrase/PORCN-class trials.

biomarkers.name: TP53 R273
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Specify the R273 substitution (R273H vs R273C vs R273L vs R273S). R273H and R273C are gain-of-function mutants with distinct chaperone (HSP90) and structural-rescue (PRIMA-1/APR-246-class, arsenic-trioxide derivatives) pharmacology profiles.

biomarkers.name: PIK3CA M1043I
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Confirm M1043I as somatic and kinase-domain-activating; relevant for PI3K-alpha-selective inhibitors (alpelisib, inavolisib) and AKT/mTOR-axis strategies; M1043 is a recurrent but non-canonical hotspot relative to H1047R/E545K/E542K.

biomarkers.name: SMAD4 R361H
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Confirm R361H as MH2-domain DNA-binding hotspot; loss-of-function disrupts TGF-beta tumor-suppressor signaling and is associated with peritoneal-spread biology and worse prognosis in CRC.

biomarkers.name: 20q11 amplification (BCL2L1/TOP1 co-amplified)
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Define amplification boundaries: 20q11.21 (BCL2L1, TOP1) vs broader 20q gain including 20q13 (ZNF217, MYBL2, AURKA). BCL2L1 amplification supports BCL-xL-directed strategies (navitoclax-class, PROTAC degraders); TOP1 amplification supports irinotecan/topotecan sensitivity rationale.

biomarkers.name: MSI status
biomarkers.decision_resolution: MSI-H/dMMR required for tumor-agnostic ICI (pembrolizumab, dostarlimab); MSS effectively excludes single-agent ICI from the standard pathway.

biomarkers.name: TMB
biomarkers.decision_resolution: TMB ≥10 mut/Mb required for tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab label; 'low' fails that gate. Capture the exact mut/Mb number for trial eligibility.

biomarkers.name: PD-L1
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Capture IHC clone (22C3, SP263, SP142) and scoring system (TPS/CPS) and exact value; PD-L1 has limited but non-zero relevance for CRC ICI combinations.

biomarkers.name: HER2 (ERBB2) amplification
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Decision-grade for mCRC: HER2 amplification (IHC 3+ or ISH ratio ≥2.0, or NGS amplification) gates tucatinib + trastuzumab (MOUNTAINEER label) and trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) off-label use. Must be checked.

biomarkers.name: BRAF V600E
biomarkers.decision_resolution: BRAF V600E status gates encorafenib + cetuximab (BEACON label). Co-occurrence with KRAS A59T would be unusual but must be excluded explicitly rather than presumed wild-type.

biomarkers.name: NRAS / HRAS
biomarkers.decision_resolution: RAS-family co-mutation status (NRAS, HRAS) gates anti-EGFR eligibility alongside KRAS. Confirm full RAS panel was clean apart from KRAS A59T.

biomarkers.name: Consensus molecular subtype (CMS) / CDX2
biomarkers.decision_resolution: CMS1-4 (immune / canonical / metabolic / mesenchymal) and CDX2 IHC are prognostic and therapy-stratifying. Peritoneal-dominant disease with SMAD4 loss suggests possible CMS4 (mesenchymal) - if available it sharpens TGF-beta-axis and stromal-targeting rationale.

current_therapy: FOLFIRI + bevacizumab (Avastin); planned cytoreductive surgery + HIPEC after systemic-therapy completion

targetable_features.rationale: Non-canonical KRAS allele. Not directly addressed by G12C-selective (sotorasib, adagrasib) or G12D-selective (MRTX1133) inhibitors, but plausibly within reach of pan-KRAS / RAS(ON) inhibitors (RMC-6236, RMC-9805, divarasib-class) and pan-RAS-pathway downstream blockade (SHP2 inhibitors RMC-4630/TNO155, MEK inhibitors, ERK inhibitors). Anti-EGFR eligibility depends on whether A59T is treated as a RAS-activating mutation by current consensus - generally yes, but worth surfacing as a research question.

Activating PI3K-alpha alteration supports PI3K-alpha selective inhibitors (alpelisib, inavolisib) in combination strategies, AKT inhibitors (capivasertib, ipatasertib), and mTOR-axis approaches. Co-occurrence with KRAS activation argues for vertical (PI3K + MEK) or horizontal (PI3K + downstream KRAS-pathway) combination biology - higher-toxicity profile but mechanistically rational.

Canonical CRC tumor-suppressor loss. Wnt-pathway-directed approaches remain investigational: tankyrase inhibitors, PORCN inhibitors (LGK974/WNT974), beta-catenin/TCF disruptors, frizzled-directed antibodies. Mostly trial-only territory but worth surfacing.

Specific p53 hotspot with emerging pharmacology: structural reactivators (APR-246/eprenetapopt, arsenic-trioxide derivatives), HSP90 inhibitors that destabilize mutant p53, and synthetic-lethal approaches (ATR inhibitors in TP53-null context). R273H particularly studied.

Loss-of-function in TGF-beta tumor-suppressor signaling - associated with peritoneal-dominant CRC biology and worse prognosis. Opens rationale for TGF-beta-axis modulation (bintrafusp alfa-class bifunctionals, anti-TGF-beta antibodies) and stromal-remodeling strategies; also a candidate biomarker for response to immunotherapy combinations that target TGF-beta-mediated immune exclusion.

BCL2L1 (BCL-xL) amplification supports BCL-xL-directed strategies (navitoclax, BCL-xL-selective PROTAC degraders DT2216-class) - relevant given anti-apoptotic dependence often correlates with chemotherapy resistance. TOP1 amplification supports continued irinotecan sensitivity rationale (FOLFIRI already in use) and potentially camptothecin-payload ADCs (e.g. T-DXd, datopotamab deruxtecan, sacituzumab govitecan) if a target antigen lights up.

Decision-relevant negative finding - excludes tumor-agnostic ICI on MSI-H or TMB-high labels and flags single-agent PD-1/PD-L1 as low-yield. Pushes immunotherapy thinking toward combination strategies (ICI + MEK, ICI + TGF-beta, ICI + bevacizumab continuation, ICI + radiation/HIPEC abscopal logic) and trial-only contexts.

Loco-regional disease control via cytoreductive surgery + HIPEC defines a window in which systemic targeted therapy can be sequenced. Choice of HIPEC agent (mitomycin C, oxaliplatin, irinotecan-based regimens) interacts with prior FOLFIRI exposure and with the BCL2L1/TOP1 amplification biology. Surfaces as a sequencing question rather than a drug-class question.
